title: Advanced useRouter: Shallow Routing & URL Manipulation
description: Update the URL without triggering data re-fetching and preserve page state.

slides.title: Beyond Simple Navigation 🧭
slides.content:
# What is Shallow Routing?

Normally, `router.push('/post/123')` runs data fetching methods again (if using SSR).

Shallow routing lets you change the URL **without** re‑running `getServerSideProps`, `getStaticProps`, or `getInitialProps`.

```jsx
router.push('/?counter=10', undefined, { shallow: true });
```

You keep the same page component mounted, but the URL updates and you can read the new query params.

slides.title: Shallow Routing Example (pages/search.js)
slides.content: Add a filter to the URL without fetching new data.

quizData.question: What is the main effect of setting `shallow: true` in `router.push`?

options.text: It changes the URL without re‑running data fetching methods
It only works on the client
It replaces the current page with an empty one

quizData.explanation: Shallow routing updates the URL and makes the new query available, but Next.js skips calling `getServerSideProps`/`getStaticProps` for that page.

slides.title: Manipulating Query Params 🧪
Multiple Filters (pages/products.js)
slides.content: Keep all active filters in the URL without page refresh.

quizData.question: When using shallow routing to update a query parameter, what must you do to keep the existing params?

options.text: Spread the existing `router.query` into the new query object
You can't keep them; shallow routing resets all params

quizData.explanation: You must manually spread `router.query` into the new query object to preserve existing parameters.

slides.title: Shallow Routing Limitations ⚠️
slides.content: Shallow routing only works for URL changes on the **same page**. If you navigate to a different page (different pathname), it will still run data fetching. It's meant for in‑page parameter updates, not cross‑page navigation.
